toc.title: A one-page review of the whole course

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • See the whole exam on one page: domains, weights and where each topic lives
  • Tell look-alike services apart in pairs and sets
  • Use need-to-service choosers for questions that describe a requirement
  • Recall the lists the exam likes, and the terms that trip people up

2A one-page review of the whole course

Running case

Lantern and Loom's Final Review

  • Lantern and Loom's platform is now secure, resilient, fast and lean
  • Before the exam, you want one page per topic, not fourteen modules
  • Some look-alikes keep getting mixed up: SQS and SNS, peering and Transit Gateway, Multi-AZ and read replicas
  • Your job: review quickly, and fix the confusions that cost points

The Exam on One Page

Domain and weight Modules Core ideas
Secure Architectures (30%) 1 to 3 IAM, SCPs, KMS, WAF, Shield, encryption, compliance
Resilient Architectures (26%) 4 and 5 Decoupling, Multi-AZ, disaster recovery strategies
High-Performing (24%) 6 to 10 Storage, compute, databases, network and edge, ingestion
Cost-Optimized (20%) 11 to 14 Storage classes, Savings Plans and Spot, NAT and endpoints
  • 65 questions (50 scored, 15 unscored), 130 minutes, 720 to pass on a scale of 100 to 1,000

Exam tip: Security carries the most weight at 30 percent, yet cost is still one question in five.

Look-Alikes: Security and Identity

Look-alikes Tell them apart
IAM user, role, Identity Center Long-term keys; temporary credentials assumed; workforce single sign-on
SCP, permissions boundary, identity policy Account guardrail, never grants; cap on one identity; grants access
KMS, CloudHSM, ACM, Secrets Manager Managed keys; dedicated HSM; TLS certificates; rotating secrets
WAF, Shield, GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie Web rules; DDoS; threat detection; vulnerability scans; sensitive data in S3
CloudTrail, Config, CloudWatch Who called the API; configuration history; metrics and logs
Security group, network ACL Stateful, instance; stateless, subnet

Exam tip: Say the one-line job of each service; the exam describes the job, not the name.

Look-Alikes: Decoupling and Integration

Look-alikes Tell them apart
SQS, SNS, EventBridge Queue, pulled by one consumer; fan-out push; event bus with rules
Standard vs FIFO queue At-least-once, best-effort order; ordered, no duplicates
Kinesis Data Streams, Firehose, MSK Ordered shards, custom consumers; delivery to S3 and more; managed Kafka
Step Functions vs SQS Orchestrate steps; buffer messages
ALB, NLB, Gateway LB Layer 7; layer 4, static IPs; inline appliances
API Gateway, Amazon MQ Managed API front door; ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ for migrated apps

Exam tip: Loose coupling means a queue, topic or event bus between the parts.

Look-Alikes: Resilience and Recovery

Look-alikes Tell them apart
Multi-AZ, read replica, Multi-Region High availability, standby; scale reads; disaster recovery across Regions
Backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active RTO from hours to seconds; cost rises each step
RPO, RTO Data you can lose; time to recover
Route 53 failover, latency, weighted Health-check switch; fastest Region; traffic split
Aurora Global Database, DynamoDB global tables Cross-Region relational replicas; multi-Region tables
AWS Backup, Elastic Disaster Recovery Policy-based backups; continuous server replication

Exam tip: Match the RTO and RPO to the cheapest strategy that meets them.

Look-Alikes: Storage and Databases

Look-alikes Tell them apart
S3, EBS, EFS, FSx Object; block for one instance; shared Linux files; Windows, Lustre, ONTAP, OpenZFS
RDS, Aurora Managed engines; cloud-native, six copies in three AZs, up to 15 replicas
DynamoDB, DAX, ElastiCache Key-value; microsecond cache for DynamoDB; in-memory cache for others
Redshift, Athena Warehouse; SQL on S3, pay per query
Timestream, Keyspaces, DocumentDB, Neptune Time series; Cassandra; MongoDB-compatible; graph
DataSync, Transfer Family, Storage Gateway, Snow Online bulk; SFTP; hybrid cache; offline

Exam tip: Pick the data model first, then the service.

Look-Alikes: Compute, Network and Edge

Look-alikes Tell them apart
EC2, Lambda, Fargate Servers; functions up to 15 minutes; containers without servers
ECS, EKS AWS-native orchestration; Kubernetes
CloudFront, Global Accelerator Caches HTTP content; static anycast IPs, TCP and UDP
Peering, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink Two VPCs; hub for many; one service privately
Direct Connect, Site-to-Site VPN Dedicated private link; encrypted over the internet
Gateway endpoint, interface endpoint S3 and DynamoDB, free; PrivateLink, hourly plus per GB

Exam tip: Static IPs and no caching: Global Accelerator. Cache it: CloudFront.

Look-Alikes: Ingestion and Analytics

Look-alikes Tell them apart
Glue, EMR, Athena Serverless ETL and catalog; Hadoop and Spark clusters; SQL on S3
Lake Formation Permissions and governance for a data lake
QuickSight, OpenSearch Dashboards; search and log analytics
AppFlow, DMS SaaS data flows; database migration and replication
Kinesis, MSK, Firehose Streaming in, Kafka, delivery
Data formats Parquet and ORC are columnar; CSV and JSON are rows

Exam tip: Query it where it sits: Athena. Move and clean it: Glue. Visualize it: QuickSight.

Service Chooser: Secure and Resilient

The need Think…
Temporary access for an app to S3 An IAM role
Encrypt with keys you control and audit KMS customer managed key
Block web exploits; absorb DDoS WAF; Shield
Limit what member accounts can do An SCP in Organizations
Survive an AZ failure Multi-AZ plus Auto Scaling
Survive a Region loss Cross-Region replication plus Route 53 failover
Buffer a traffic spike SQS

Exam tip: Name the verb in the need (encrypt, block, buffer, fail over), then the service.

Service Chooser: High-Performing and Cost-Optimized

The need Think…
Cache static content worldwide CloudFront
Fixed IPs with fast failover Global Accelerator
Low-latency key-value at scale DynamoDB, with DAX
Shared Windows files FSx for Windows File Server
Steady baseline compute Savings Plans; restartable work on Spot
Unknown S3 access; rare access Intelligent-Tiering; Glacier by lifecycle
Private servers reading S3 A gateway endpoint

Exam tip: Cost clues: steady, unknown, rare, restartable, idle.

Lists and Terms the Exam Likes

  • Well-Architected pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability
  • DR strategies, cheapest first: backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active
  • S3 classes, hot to cold: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant, Flexible, Deep Archive
  • Purchase options: On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Spot
  • Terms: RPO and RTO; horizontal and vertical scaling; stateless and stateful; eventual and strong consistency

Exam tip: Lists are easy points: say each one aloud from memory.

3Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
One page four domains, 65 questions, 130 minutes, 720 to pass
Look-alikes learn the one-line job of each service; the exam describes the job
Choosers name the verb in the need, then the service
Lists pillars, DR strategies, S3 classes, purchase options
Terms RPO, RTO, horizontal, vertical, stateless, eventual consistency
